_howto: Employee Master how-to guides (listed under How-to guides in the ? menu). mode click = the user clicks the real button. optional = skipped when that field isn't on screen. Never reuse a step id.

guides.title: Create an employee
guides.blurb: Add a new employee, with what each field on all five tabs is for.

steps.title: Active Personnel
steps.text: New employees are added from the Active Personnel list. Click it.

steps.title: Create Employee
steps.text: Click Create Employee. Nothing is saved until you click Create Employee again at the bottom of the form, so it's safe to follow along.

steps.title: Required fields
steps.text:
Fields marked with a red * must be filled in: PIN, First Name, Last Name, ID/Passport No, Department, Group Start Date and Default Shift. Everything else is optional and can be added later on Edit.

The Display PIN / ID is the employee's number on lists, reports and devices. It must be unique.

steps.title: Names
steps.text: First Name and Last Name are required. Title, Initials, Second Name and Known As (the name they go by) are optional.

steps.title: ID or Passport No (identity)
steps.text:
Required. Their South African ID number or, if they don't have one, their passport number. This is their identity number on lists, reports and exports.

If you type a passport number here, Passport Number on the Employment tab fills in by itself.

steps.title: Personal details
steps.text: Date of Birth, Gender, Marital Status, Language, Ethnic Group and Nationality. Optional, kept for HR records and reporting.

steps.title: Contact Information
steps.text: Click Add Contact, choose the type (Cell, Home, Business, Email or Other) and type the detail. One of each type is saved. Keep the cell number and email address correct.

steps.title: Department
steps.text: Required. The department decides which clocking devices the employee is sent to (through Access Roles and Settings > Access Zones, or their Access Control levels), where they sit in the hierarchy, and how they're grouped in reports.

steps.title: Job details
steps.text: Job Title shows on the list and reports. Job Grade is optional, and Occupation (Legacy) is an older field kept for existing data.

steps.title: Group Start Date
steps.text: Required. Their first day. If it's in the future, they wait under the Pending start filter. On that day they become active automatically and are sent to their clocking devices.

steps.title: Employee Type
steps.text: Permanent, Seasonal, or one of your own types from Custom Attributes.

steps.title: Scheduled End Date
steps.text: For anyone with a known last day, of any employee type. They are terminated automatically on this date (reason End of Contract). Leave it empty if there's no end date.

steps.title: Cost Centre
steps.text: Links the employee to a cost centre for financial reporting (set up in Departments > Cost Centres).

steps.title: Previous Period Worked
steps.text: For someone who has worked here before: the date of their earlier period of employment.

steps.title: Date Engaged
steps.text: The date they were engaged, if different from the Group Start Date.

steps.title: RFID Card Number
steps.text: Their access card number, if they clock or open doors with a card. It's sent to their devices with their name and PIN.

steps.title: Passport (foreign nationals)
steps.text: For foreign nationals only. Passport Number fills in by itself from the identity number on the Personal tab, so just check it, then add the Passport Country, Passport Expiry and Work Permit Expiry. Leave this block empty for South African ID holders.

steps.title: Reports To
steps.text: Their direct manager. Type a name or PIN to find them.

steps.title: Head of Department
steps.text: Tick this if the person heads a department, then choose which department(s).

steps.title: Tax & Statutory
steps.text: Tax Number, Tax Office, Tax Status, UIF Status, and up to three tax directives with a Directive %. Filled in for payroll.

steps.title: Statutory flags
steps.text: Legally Retired, Seasonal Worker and Exclude for OID (leave them out of the Compensation Fund / OID returns). Tick only what applies.

steps.title: Default Shift
steps.text:
Required. The shift they normally work, shown with its start and end times (from Time & Attendance > Shift Rules). It drives their roster and how their clockings are worked out: late arrival, early departure and overtime.

The Effective Date Range next to it is only needed when you change a shift later, on Edit.

steps.title: Overtime Eligibility
steps.text: How their extra hours are treated: Paid Overtime, Unpaid Overtime or Time-Off in Lieu.

steps.title: Default Working Days
steps.text: Tick the days this person normally works. If you tick none, Monday to Friday is used. Days that aren't ticked are their rest days: they aren't expected at work, and time worked on a rest day counts as overtime that needs approval.

steps.title: Custom OT Rule
steps.text: An overtime rule just for this person, from Time & Attendance > Overtime Rules. Leave it on No Rule to use the normal rules.

steps.title: Payroll Period
steps.text: The pay period they belong to, such as weekly or monthly. Their timesheets and payroll exports follow this period.

steps.title: Custom Attributes
steps.text: Your company's own fields, created in Custom Attributes (for example Boot Size or Tractor Licence). Fill in any that apply; empty ones are skipped.

steps.title: Allowances
steps.text: Whether they qualify for the Night Allowance and the Standby Allowance. Both are ticked by default.

steps.title: Wage
steps.text: Wage Type (Hourly Rate or Fixed Salary), Rate/Amount, the date it's Valid From, and Pay Method (EFT, Cash or Cheque). Employee Costs uses exactly this wage type and rate.

steps.title: Medical aid beneficiaries
steps.text: Click Add for each dependant on their medical aid: name, relationship, date of birth, and whether they're covered.

steps.title: Emergency contacts
steps.text: Click Add for each person to contact in an emergency.

steps.title: Fund & Benefit Memberships
steps.text: Click Add for each fund or benefit they belong to.

steps.title: Addresses
steps.text: Click Add Address and choose the type: Residential, Postal or Work (one of each is saved). Use Clone on a row to start another type from the same address.

steps.title: Banking details
steps.text: Bank Name, Account Number, Branch Code and Account Type, for paying them by EFT.

steps.title: Attachments
steps.text: Upload a copy of their ID or passport, their work permit and a bank confirmation letter (a picture or PDF). They are saved with the employee and can be viewed on their profile.

steps.title: Create Employee
steps.text:
Saves the new employee with everything you filled in. Straight after that:

• They are sent to the clocking devices their department and access allow.
• A self-service login is created for them. Their username and first password are their PIN, so ask them to change it.

This guide hasn't created anything: close the form if you were only practising.

guides.title: Every field on an employee profile
guides.blurb: Open a profile and go through each tab and field, including Default Shift and working days.

steps.title: Active Personnel
steps.text: Employee profiles are opened from the Active Personnel list. Click it to open the list.

steps.title: Open a profile
steps.text: Click Edit on any employee. Nothing is saved unless you click Save Profile at the end, so it's safe to look around.

steps.title: Profile photo
steps.text: View, upload, crop or remove the employee's photo. This is their profile photo across the system; the Missing Photo report lists anyone without one.

steps.title: Find a field
steps.text: Type the name of any field, like shift or bank, to jump straight to it on whichever tab it's on.

steps.title: Display PIN / ID
steps.text: The employee's number as it appears on lists, reports and exports. It must be filled in and should be unique.

steps.title: Names
steps.text: First Name and Last Name are required. Title, Initials, Second Name and Known As (the name they actually go by) are optional.

steps.title: ID or Passport No (identity)
steps.text:
Required. Their South African ID number or, if they don't have one, their passport number. This is their identity number on lists, reports and exports.

If you type a passport number here, Passport Number on the Employment tab fills in by itself.

steps.title: Personal details
steps.text: Date of Birth, Gender, Marital Status, Language, Ethnic Group and Nationality. All optional; they are kept for HR records and reporting.

steps.title: Contact Information
steps.text: One row per type: Cell, Home, Business, Email and Other. Add a row, choose its type and type the detail. Keep the cell number and email address up to date.

steps.title: Department
steps.text: Required. The department decides which clocking devices they can use (through Access Roles), where they sit in the hierarchy, and how they are grouped in reports.

steps.title: Transfer Effective Date
steps.text: Only appears when you change the department. The date the move takes effect. Leave from that date is measured against the new department.

steps.title: Job details
steps.text: Job Title shows on the employee list and reports. Job Grade is optional, and Occupation (Legacy) is an older field kept for existing data.

steps.title: Group Start Date
steps.text: Required. Their first day with the group. If it's still in the future, they show under the Pending start filter until that day.

steps.title: Employee Type
steps.text: Permanent, Seasonal, or one of your own types from Custom Attributes.

steps.title: Scheduled End Date
steps.text: For fixed-term people: the employee is automatically scheduled for termination on this date.

steps.title: Cost Centre
steps.text: Links the employee to a cost centre for financial reporting. Cost centres are set up in Departments > Cost Centres.

steps.title: Previous Period Worked
steps.text: The date of an earlier period of employment, for someone who has worked here before.

steps.title: RFID Card Number
steps.text: The number of their access card, if they clock or open doors with a card.

steps.title: Passport (foreign nationals)
steps.text: For foreign nationals only. Passport Number fills in by itself from the identity number on the Personal tab, so just check it, then add the Passport Country, Passport Expiry and Work Permit Expiry. Leave this block empty for South African ID holders.

steps.title: Reports To
steps.text: Their direct manager. Type a name or PIN to find them. This shows on the employee list and builds their reporting line.

steps.title: Head of Department
steps.text: Tick this if the person heads a department, then choose which department(s) they head.

steps.title: Tax & Statutory
steps.text: Tax Number, Tax Office, Tax Status, UIF Status, and up to three tax directives with a Directive %. Filled in for payroll.

steps.title: Statutory flags
steps.text: Legally Retired, Seasonal Worker, and Exclude for OID (leave them out of the Compensation Fund / OID returns). Tick only what applies.

steps.title: Default Shift
steps.text: The shift they normally work, shown with its start and end times. Shifts are set up in Time & Attendance > Shift Rules. This drives their roster and how their clockings are worked out: late arrival, early departure and overtime.

steps.title: Effective Date Range
steps.text: Only needed when you change the Default Shift: choose the start and end dates the new shift applies to on the roster. The start can be up to 30 days in the past. If it is in the past, run the Nightly Analyzer for those dates afterwards so their attendance is recalculated.

steps.title: Overtime Eligibility
steps.text: How their extra hours are treated: Paid Overtime, Unpaid Overtime or Time-Off in Lieu.

steps.title: Default Working Days
steps.text: The days this person normally works (Monday to Friday unless you change it). Days that aren't ticked are their rest days: they aren't expected at work, and time worked on a rest day counts as overtime that needs approval.

steps.title: Custom OT Rule
steps.text: An overtime rule just for this person, from Time & Attendance > Overtime Rules. Leave it on No Rule to use the normal rules.

steps.title: Payroll Period
steps.text: The pay period they belong to, such as weekly or monthly. Their timesheets and payroll exports follow this period.

steps.title: Leave balances
steps.text: Their balance for each paid leave type. You can adjust a balance here.

steps.title: Leave history
steps.text: The leave they have taken.

steps.title: Custom Attributes
steps.text: Your company's own fields, created in Custom Attributes.

steps.title: ZKTeco Access Levels
steps.text: Access levels from your ZKTeco system for this person, on top of what their department gives them.

steps.title: Allowances
steps.text: Whether they qualify for the Night Allowance and the Standby Allowance.

steps.title: Wage
steps.text: Wage Type (Hourly Rate or Fixed Salary), Rate/Amount, the date it's Valid From, and Pay Method (EFT, Cash or Cheque). Employee Costs uses exactly this wage type and rate.

steps.title: Medical aid beneficiaries
steps.text: Dependants on their medical aid: name, relationship and date of birth.

steps.title: Emergency contacts
steps.text: Who to contact in an emergency.

steps.title: Fund & Benefit Memberships
steps.text: The funds and benefits they belong to.

steps.title: Infringements & performance
steps.text: Infringements, warnings and performance notes recorded in HR Management.

steps.title: Employment Contracts
steps.text: Their employment contracts.

steps.title: Reporting Structure
steps.text: Who they report to, all the way up the line.

steps.title: Addresses
steps.text: One row per type: Residential, Postal and Work. Use Clone on a row to start another type from the same address.

steps.title: Banking details
steps.text: Bank Name, Account Number, Branch Code and Account Type, for paying them by EFT.

steps.title: Attachments
steps.text: Upload their ID or passport, work permit and bank confirmation letter (a picture or PDF). Once a document is saved, Attached shows under it, with View to open it. Uploading a new file replaces the old one when you save.

steps.title: Audit & History
steps.text: Every change made to this profile: when, what and by whom.

steps.title: Save Profile
steps.text: Saves your changes. This guide hasn't changed anything, so close the profile without saving if you were only looking.

guides.title: Terminate and reinstate an employee
guides.blurb: End someone's employment on a chosen date, then bring a former employee back.

steps.title: Active Personnel
steps.text: Terminations start from the Active Personnel list. Click it.

steps.title: Terminate
steps.text:
Click Terminate on any employee. Nothing happens until you click Lock in System, so it's safe to follow along.

To terminate several people at once, tick them in the list and use Terminate on the toolbar instead. It opens the same form.

steps.title: Check the name
steps.text: Make sure this is the right person before you go any further.

steps.title: Termination Date
steps.text:
Their termination date. It can be today or a date still to come. On that date the profile moves to Terminated Records, and at midnight they are removed from your ZKTeco devices automatically.

Until then they stay active, and they appear on the Pending Terminations report.

steps.title: Reason
steps.text: Why they left: Resigned, Relocated, Dismissed, Retrenched, End of Season, End of Contract or Deceased. The reason is used by the Reason filter in Terminated Records.

steps.title: Your own reason
steps.text: If none of the reasons fit, click + Add Custom Reason. Your reason is added to the list for next time.

steps.title: Lock in System
steps.text:
Schedules the termination. This guide hasn't changed anything: click Cancel if you were only looking.

Next, let's see how to bring someone back.

steps.title: Terminated Records
steps.text: Former employees are here. Click it.

steps.title: Reinstate
steps.text:
Click Reinstate on any former employee. Again, nothing happens until you confirm.

To bring back several people, for example at the start of a season, tick them and use Bulk Reinstate.

steps.title: Reinstatement Date
steps.text: The day they come back. On that date they become active in Active Personnel automatically, with their history kept, and are sent back to their clocking devices.

steps.title: Reinstate
steps.text:
Schedules their return. Click Cancel if you were only looking.

Also on each former employee's row: Edit Details corrects a termination date or reason, and View History shows every termination and reinstatement.

guides.title: Import employees from Excel
guides.blurb: Fill in a template, check it with a dry run, then add or update many employees at once.

steps.title: Active Personnel
steps.text: The import starts from Active Personnel. Click it.

steps.title: Start with a template
steps.text:
Custom Blank Template gives you an Excel file with the columns you tick. PIN, First Name, Last Name and Department are always included, and you can save your choice as a preset. Put one employee per row.

Custom Export Data gives the same file already filled with your employees, which is handy for updating many people at once.

steps.title: Data Import Wizard
steps.text: When your file is filled in, click Data Import Wizard.

steps.title: Choose your file
steps.text: Choose your completed .xlsx file. The wizard opens as soon as you pick it.

steps.title: Row containing headers
steps.text: Which row of your file holds the column names. Rows above it are ignored. The preview further down updates when you change it, so you can check it's right.

steps.title: Date format
steps.text: How dates are written in your file. Leave it on Auto-Detect for normal Excel dates. Choose DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD if dates were typed in as text.

steps.title: Column Mapping
steps.text: Check each column in your file is matched to the right employee field.

steps.title: Raw File Preview
steps.text: The first rows of your file as the wizard reads them. If the columns look shifted, the header row number above is probably wrong.

steps.title: Run Validation (Dry Run)
steps.text: Checks every row without saving anything. Click it when the mapping looks right.

steps.title: Validation results
steps.text: How many rows will create New Profiles, how many will Update employees already on the system, and how many have Errors and will be skipped.

steps.title: Row by row
steps.text: The result for each row, with the reason for every error. Fix those rows in your file and run the wizard again, or use Back to Mapping to change the mapping.

steps.title: Commit to Database
steps.text: Saves the new and updated employees. It asks you to confirm first. Nothing has been saved yet: use Cancel Import if you were only practising.

guides.title: Move employees to another department
guides.blurb: Two ways: one employee from their profile, or many at once with Move Department. Both ask for the date the transfer takes effect.

steps.title: Two ways to move people
steps.text:
There are two ways to move employees to another department, both from Active Personnel:
Way 1 - one employee: open their profile and change the Department.
Way 2 - many at once: tick them in the list and use Move Department.
Click Active Personnel to start with Way 1.

steps.title: Way 1: open the profile
steps.text: Click Edit on the employee you want to move. Nothing is saved until you click Save Profile, so it is safe to follow along.

steps.title: Choose the new department
steps.text: On the Employment tab, click Department and pick the department they are moving to.

steps.title: Transfer Effective Date
steps.text: Appears as soon as the department changes. Enter the date the move takes effect - it is required. Their leave and history count against the new department from that date.

steps.title: Save Profile
steps.text: Saves the move. The transfer shows in Audit & History. If you were only practising, close the profile without saving.

steps.title: Way 2: tick the employees
steps.text: To move many people at once, tick the box next to each employee (or the box in the heading for everyone on the page). A blue bar appears above the list.

steps.title: Move Department
steps.text: Click Move Department on the blue bar.

steps.title: New Department
steps.text: Pick the department everyone you ticked is moving to. Leave it on Do Not Change to keep their department (for example to change only their team).

steps.title: Transfer Effective Date
steps.text: Required when you change the department: the date the move takes effect for all of them.

steps.title: Custom Team (optional)
steps.text: You can move them into a Custom Team at the same time, or remove them from their current team. Leave it on Do Not Change Team otherwise.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Moves everyone you ticked in one go. If you were only practising, click Cancel instead.

guides.title: Run, filter and export a report
guides.blurb: Pick a report, narrow it down, choose the columns and export it to Excel or PDF.

steps.title: Data Reports
steps.text: Reports are under Data Reports. Click it.

steps.title: Pick a report
steps.text: Choose a report, e.g. Full Employee Details or Missing Info Report. It runs as soon as you pick it; the line under the bar says what it shows.

steps.title: Open the filters
steps.text: Click Filters.

steps.title: Department
steps.text: Only people in this department. Leave it on All Departments for everyone.

steps.title: Date range
steps.text: Optional Date From and Date To: they apply to start dates (or termination dates on the termination reports). Clear Filters removes them all.

steps.title: Apply Filters
steps.text: Runs the report again with these filters. They show as tags next to the buttons; the x on a tag removes it.

steps.title: Choose the columns
steps.text: Click Columns any time to tick the columns you want and drag them into your order. Each report remembers your choice.

steps.title: Narrow it down
steps.text: Type in the box under a heading to keep only matching rows, e.g. a job title. Every word you type must be in that column.

steps.title: Sort and move columns
steps.text: Click a heading to sort (A to Z, again for Z to A, a third time back). Drag a heading left or right to move the column.

steps.title: Export
steps.text: Click Export.

steps.title: Excel or PDF
steps.text: Pick Export to Excel or Export to PDF. The file has exactly the columns shown, in your order, and only the rows the searches leave.

guides.title: Add custom fields and fill them in bulk
guides.blurb: Create your own fields (e.g. Boot Size), then fill them for many employees at once with the import template.

steps.title: Custom Attributes
steps.text: Your own employee fields are under Custom Attributes. Click it.

steps.title: Add a field
steps.text: Click Add Attribute.

steps.title: Name and type
steps.text: Give it a name (e.g. Boot Size) and pick the Data Type: Text, Number, Date or Yes / No. Save adds it to every employee profile. Nothing is saved until you click Save.

steps.title: Done
steps.text: Save it, or click Cancel if you were only practising.

steps.title: Which employees
steps.text: To fill the fields in bulk, first choose who goes in the file: click Filters for one department or PIN, or leave it for everyone.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Click Data Tools.

steps.title: Download Import Template
steps.text: An Excel file with your employees and an empty column per field. Fill it in (keep the PIN column as it is).

steps.title: Import Excel
steps.text: Load the filled-in file. The values go onto each employee's profile.

steps.title: Export Data
steps.text: Everyone's current values: check them, or change them in Excel and import the file back the same way.

steps.title: Edit or deactivate
steps.text: Change a field's name or type with the pencil; Deactivate hides it everywhere but keeps its values - bring it back from the Deactivated tab.
